CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current posture and keep diplomatic channels open while preparing a calibrated, proportional response if the US follows through on broad Section 301 action. Do not preemptively escalate, but also make no concessions on core technology-transfer principles, which are central to our industrial and self-sufficiency strategy. Signal willingness to negotiate within the WTO multilateral framework even as we stand firm on the substance.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is elevated but not yet existential. The Section 301 investigation (initiated Aug 2017) directly targets our technology-transfer and IP practices, threatening the export economy and our tech-autonomy model, and US sectoral tariffs under Section 201 (solar panels, washing machines) already landed in Jan 2018. However, at this date no broad China-specific tariffs have been imposed, and reports suggest remedies could be announced soon. Critically, our macro position is strong — GDP grew 6.9% in 2017 (fastest in seven years), exports rose ~11%, and the economy held up in Feb 2018 — so the export base and financial stability that would buffer a trade shock are intact. This justifies a moderate positive threat score (+0.4) rather than a higher one. Because escalation now would risk provoking a full-scale trade war that could harm our export economy and because the opponent has made no matching concession offer, China should hold and negotiate rather than escalate or concede. A measured, firm stance preserves leverage on tech-transfer while leaving room to avoid the worst outcome.
key_factors: Section 301 investigation into China IP/tech-transfer still open, broad tariffs not yet imposed
Section 201 tariffs on solar and washing machines already hit China (Jan 2018)
Trump Beijing visit (Nov 2017) produced commercial MOUs but no structural concessions
China GDP grew 6.9% in 2017, fastest in 7 years; exports up ~11%; economy holds up Feb 2018
China cannot concede on tech-transfer without undermining industrial-policy/self-sufficiency goals, but should avoid provoking full trade war

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump signs memorandum directing USTR to investigate China's IP and technology-transfer practices under Section 301.
Trump visits Beijing; large package of commercial deals announced (many MOUs). No substantive concessions on structural IP / tech-transfer issues.
Trump approves Section 201 safeguard tariffs on solar panels and washing machines (China among suppliers hit). First major tariff action.
China reports fastest economic growth in 7 years, GDP up 6.9% in 2017; exports grew nearly 11%.
USTR expected to announce affirmative Section 301 finding and remedy recommendations soon; Commerce Ministry warns it will take all necessary measures to safeguard interests.
